# PV03 / draft-to-full native video-reference pilot

1280x736 / 56 frames / same four images, Guide 0, seed and 8-step profile as AC05.
Video 1 is the exact PV01 896x512 generated draft.
Prompt roles and action phases follow the actual draft, including its aiming hold and height variation.
This is not a text-identical video-only ablation or deterministic upscale.

widgets_values_named.text:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [Add Guide for MiniMax H3](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15439)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the **MiniMax H3 Reference to Video** node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

On top of that, chained **Add Guide for MiniMax H3** nodes pin extra stills (or short clips, and optional audio) onto specific frames of the *output* timeline. The model can address guides anywhere on a continuous time axis, not only the first and last frame. That is the multi-frame / keyframe path in this graph.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios** on **MiniMax H3 Reference to Video**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips. These are semantic references. Name them in connection order as `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`. They do not sit on a timeline by themselves.
- **prompt** (**Input Text (Prompt)**): reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio. In this template, also name each later picture as a shot's first frame or keyframe, and cut to it at the matching timestamp in `detailed_description`.
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via **Resolution Selector (Size)**
- **duration (seconds)** (**Float (Duration)**): converted to a valid frame `length` by the **Math Expression** node

**Multi-frame guides (Add Guide for MiniMax H3)**

Each **Add Guide for MiniMax H3** anchors a guide at `frame_idx` (negative values count from the end of the video):

- a still image
- a clip (image batches snap down to the model's valid clip lengths: 5, 22, 39... frames; batches shorter than 5 frames use only the first image)
- audio, starting at the same position
- any combination. Chain several nodes (`positive` in to `positive` out) for several guides

`frame_idx` is in frames at 24fps. This template sets it from **Frame Index (Second)** through **Math Expression** `round(a * 24)` (1.5s → frame 36). The index plus the guide length must stay inside the generated `length`.

This graph wires four pictures as follows:

- **Load Image** `h3_frame_ref_1.png` → first `ref_images` input on **MiniMax H3 Reference to Video**. This is `<Picture 1>`, the identity lock and the first frame of Shot 1. There is no Add Guide at 0s; the prompt tells the model the video starts from `<Picture 1>`.
- **Load Image** `h3_frame_ref_2.png` → first **Add Guide for MiniMax H3** at **1.5s** (Shot 2 keyframe)
- **Load Image** `h3_frame_ref_3.png` → second Add Guide at **3.0s** (Shot 3 keyframe)
- **Load Image** `h3_frame_ref_4.png` → third Add Guide at **5.0s** (Shot 4 first frame)

To add more keyframes, copy the same block: **Load Image** + **Frame Index (Second)** + **Math Expression** + **Add Guide for MiniMax H3**. Keep `positive` in series (last guide → **Basic Guider**). Reuse the same video VAE, audio VAE, and `LATENT` from **MiniMax H3 Reference to Video**. Leave `audio` empty unless you also want a soundtrack anchored at that time.

`<Picture N>` tags only bind to images actually connected on `ref_images`, in that order. Pictures 2-4 here are timeline anchors only. Also plug them into extra `ref_images` slots if you want the text encoder to see them as `<Picture 2>` / `<Picture 3>` / `<Picture 4>`.

Other useful patterns from the same node: feed the first 22 frames of an existing video plus its audio into one Add Guide at `frame_idx` 0 to continue both streams, or drop a still at a mid-clip frame (for example frame 60 of 124) to force the shot to hit that frame.

## Input Assets
- [h3_frame_ref_1.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/h3_frame_ref_1.png)

- [h3_frame_ref_4.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/h3_frame_ref_4.png)


## Model Links
[🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

**vae**

- [minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors) (2.62 GB)
- [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors) (577.2 MB)

**diffusion_models**

- [minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors) (19.53 GB)

**text_encoders**

- [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors) (14.61 GB)

**loras**

- 4 steps: [minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/loras/minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors) (1.82 GB)

**embeddings**

- [10 style embeddings](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/tree/main/embeddings) (`minimaxh3_*.safetensors`), for example `minimaxh3_art_is_explosion`

## Model Storage Location

```
📂 ComfyUI/
├── 📂 models/
│   ├── 📂 vae/
│   │   ├── minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   │   └── minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
│   │   └── minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 text_encoders/
│   │   └── qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 loras/
│   │   └── minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors
│   └── 📂 embeddings/
│       └── minimaxh3_art_is_explosion.safetensors
```

## Using Prompt Embeddings

Prompt embeddings (supported since [ComfyUI#15697](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15697)) add reusable style tokens to your prompt. Download one or more embeddings from the folder above into `ComfyUI/models/embeddings/`, then reference one in the prompt text with the `embedding:` prefix and the filename without its extension, for example:

`embedding:minimaxh3_art_is_explosion`

Using an embedding is optional and the template runs fine without one.

## Report Issue

Note: Please update ComfyUI first ([guide](https://docs.comfy.org/installation/update_comfyui)) and prepare required models. Desktop/Cloud updates follow stable releases, so some nightly-supported models may not be available yet.

- Cannot run / runtime errors: [ComfyUI/issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues)
- UI / frontend issues: [ComfyUI_frontend/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/issues)
- Workflow issues: [workflow_templates/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/issues)

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is one adult Claire. <Picture 2> defines her proportions and below-collar costume: fitted gray underlayer, segmented gray armor, tactical belt, long central front fabric panel, dark cloak and armored heeled boots. <Picture 4> defines her headgear and anatomical two-handed grip: raised black hood, concealed ponytail, chestnut fringe and exact rigid sealed graphite mask with a smoked visor and one steady thin cyan arc. Her starting body pose comes from <Picture 4>. These pictures depict the same woman; the gray studio backgrounds and the different visor in <Picture 2> are outside their reference roles.
<Subject 2> is Claire's single rune carbine. <Picture 3> defines its black skeletal stock, pistol grip, circular side mechanism, segmented silver-and-black barrel housing, engraved gold inlays and cylindrical muzzle. <Picture 4> supplies the anatomical two-handed grip; <Picture 4> supplies its supported scale and initial orientation.
<Subject 3> is the empty rainy upper monastery gallery in <Picture 1>, including the foreground stone parapet, close left pillar, rear columns, broken pointed arches and cold night light.
<Picture 4> is the assembled first frame of [Shot 1], defining the exact opening camera, Claire's scale and position behind the parapet, closed cyan-arc headgear, supported two-handed aim and muzzle direction slightly beside the lens.
<Subject 4> is the visible maneuver performed by Claire in <Video 1>: one supported shot, a short aiming hold, a modest rise-and-settle of the torso and rightward travel with the carbine covering the same camera-side courtyard. It supplies the actual motion phases for <Subject 1>.
<Video 1> is the generated PV01 draft, 56 frames at 24 fps, used as the fixed-camera, timing and screen-space path reference for [Shot 1]. The target keeps the image-defined costume, rigid mask and drawn materials while reusing this motion at the same playback pace.

summary:
[reference generation + keyframe completion] Combine <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> within <Subject 3> for one silent 2.33-second continuous shot, recreating the actual visible maneuver of <Subject 4> in <Video 1>. Begin from the exact assembled composition of <Picture 4>. <Picture 1> through <Picture 4> retain their location, identity, headgear, grip and prop roles. The video supplies the shot, aiming hold, height variation and rightward trajectory at the same real-time pace.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - identity, visible costume construction and exact cyan-arc headgear retain their defined source roles; <Picture 4> supplies the active starting body pose that develops into the linked movement.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - one rigid carbine retains its design and two-handed shoulder support while moving with Claire.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the gallery's architectural identity, parapet, open floor path, cold lighting and wet materials remain consistent as Claire occupies the scene.
<Picture 4> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the opening uses its composition, character scale, supported aiming pose, closed mask and muzzle direction.
<Subject 4> (performed by <Subject 1> in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the visible action order, supported aiming orientation, torso-height phases and rightward displacement are reused.
<Video 1> ([Shot 1] motion and fixed-camera timing): fully_preserved - its temporal structure and screen-space path guide the whole shot; the detailed target appearance and first-frame composition retain their image-reference roles.

detailed_description:
Use the detailed painterly dark-fantasy anime rendering of <Picture 1> and <Picture 4>, with fine linework, cold blue-gray night colors and restrained wet-metal highlights. One fixed camera observes the gallery in a near-frontal, slightly low medium view.

[Shot 1] The opening frame corresponds to <Picture 4>. Recreate <Subject 4> from <Video 1> at its original playback pace, transferring the visible body path and supported carbine orientation into this image-defined scene. <Subject 1> is already behind the near foreground parapet of <Subject 3>, initially left of center with open room to her screen right. Her feet are supported by the gallery floor on the inner side of the stone barrier. Its upper edge conceals her lower legs, while her hood, complete mask, shoulders, both attached hands and muzzle remain readable. Her compact loaded aiming crouch follows <Picture 4>, with the fitted armor and heavy cloak construction of <Picture 2>.

She holds <Subject 2> at her anatomical right shoulder. Her right hand encloses its grip and her left supports the fore-end; bent elbows connect the same rigid weapon to her torso. The muzzle projects safely above the parapet and points slightly beside the lens toward the established off-screen lookout in the courtyard on the camera side. The long barrel is naturally foreshortened by this angle.

During the opening 0.17 seconds, Claire maintains the loaded aim shown at the beginning of <Video 1>. Around 0.17 to 0.29 seconds, one brief cyan-white flash leaves the actual muzzle of <Subject 2>, lighting the adjacent wet metal. The stock and bent arms take the compact impulse together while the supported barrel continues to cover the established camera-side courtyard.

Through approximately 0.90 seconds, retain the draft's short post-shot aiming hold with small settling motion in the connected shoulders and arms. The muzzle remains above the parapet, and the same hands stay attached to the same fore-end and grip. From about 0.90 to 1.30 seconds, the torso adjusts and begins its weight transfer as in <Video 1>; the cloak follows this limited movement with delayed folds.

Between roughly 1.30 and 1.65 seconds, reproduce the draft's modest rise and subsequent compression, with the supported rifle moving together with her shoulder. Her body then travels toward screen right along the parapet through the final 2.33-second boundary. The stationary columns make the sideways movement visible. Her muzzle continues pointing toward the same courtyard throughout this travel, while the stance and torso height follow the reference's visible phases. The final instant catches her still moving right, with her cloak trailing left and its folds drawing after the body. The architecture stays fixed, her mask stays rigid and sealed, and the single thin cyan arc remains steady. Output is silent.

# Profile

Omni NVFP4 QAD / NVFP4 AWQ encoder / original VAEs
8 steps res_multistep/simple, BasicGuider, shifts 12/3
Only Guide 0, free ending, no ControlNet, Motion Context or custom nodes.
One bounded run, no automatic retry; measure draft plus full-pass cost.
